content:
1. Pultrusion Manufacturing Technology

Pultruded grating is manufactured by pulling continuous glass fiber rovings through a resin impregnation bath, then through a precision-heated steel die that cures the resin into a constant cross-section profile. The process produces bars with highly aligned unidirectional fibers (70-75% fiber content by weight), resulting in exceptional longitudinal strength. Typical pultrusion speed: 0.5-2.0 m/min, die temperature: 150-180°C with multi-zone control.

2. Cross-Section Design & Profiles

Common pultruded grating bar profiles include: I-beam (standard for most applications), T-bar (for increased top surface area), rectangular tube (for high torsional stiffness), and custom profiles. Bar heights range from 25mm to 100mm, with wall thickness from 3mm to 8mm. Bearing bar spacing is typically 30mm, 38mm, or 50mm on center. Cross bars are typically 6mm diameter solid rods or 25×3mm flat bars, spaced at 100-150mm intervals.

3. Load Capacity & Structural Calculation

50mm deep I-bar pultruded grating at 1000mm span achieves: allowable uniform load 25 kN/m², point load capacity 5 kN at center, maximum deflection L/240. Bending strength: 350-420 MPa, elastic modulus: 20-25 GPa (longitudinal). Design calculations follow ASTM D3916 (pultruded shapes) and EUROCOMP design code. Safety factors: 2.5 for ultimate strength, 1.5 for serviceability (deflection).

4. Connection & Assembly Systems

Pultruded grating panels are assembled using: stainless steel clips (M-clip, C-clip, G-clip types), FRP bolted connections, and adhesive bonding. Clip systems allow for easy installation and removal. Recommended fastener spacing: 600mm maximum for bearing bars, 300mm for edge supports. Thermal expansion coefficient: 12-15 × 10⁻⁶ /°C (longitudinal), requiring expansion gaps of 3-5mm per panel at installation.

5. Heavy-Duty Application Trends 2026

Emerging heavy-duty applications for pultruded grating include: mining industry walkways and conveyor platforms (replacing steel in corrosive mine environments), offshore oil & gas platform decking (fire-retardant vinyl ester systems), heavy industrial flooring for forklift traffic (65mm deep I-bar rated for 3-ton forklift), bridge decking and pedestrian bridges (lightweight, corrosion-free), and renewable energy access platforms (wind turbine interiors, solar farm maintenance walkways). The heavy-duty pultruded grating segment is growing at 8.5% CAGR, outpacing the overall FRP grating market.
